heroHeadline: US Envoys Shuttle Between Moscow and Kyiv Pushing Peace Plan as Zelensky Rejects Territorial Concessions
heroSubtitle: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin for three hours on September 5 before traveling to Kyiv on September 6 for 'substantive' talks with President Zelensky, who rejected a floated US proposal for Ukraine to cede unoccupied Donetsk territory as a demilitarized zone while signaling openness to dropping Ukraine's NATO bid for binding security guarantees. A temporary pause on strikes against Moscow and Kyiv held during the shuttle diplomacy, but fighting continued elsewhere: a Russian ballistic missile strike on the Kametstal plant in Kamianske killed 5 workers on September 5, Ukrainian drones knocked out over 77% of the Ryazan oil refinery's crude-processing capacity on September 6, and Russian drone swarms hit a Zaporizhzhia shopping mall and a Pryluky tobacco factory on September 7. Separately, the IAEA brokered a seventh localized ceasefire on September 5 to let technicians repair the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant's last power line, restoring an external connection lost since August 20. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,497,980 by September 7, per the Ukrainian General Staff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
